subject.title: feat(control-ui): import Codex and Claude Code memory

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support these public Gateway and Plugin SDK contracts for discovering and importing private Codex and Claude Code memory into indexed agent workspaces?
rationale: The implementation is bounded and well-proven, but merging creates a durable API and authorization boundary around private local data that cannot be accepted solely from code correctness or CI.

options.title: Approve the bounded contract
options.body: Accept the provider-neutral, memory-only API with its current explicit selection, idempotency, workspace confinement, backup, and recovery guarantees.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep the Control UI capability but make the migration hooks private or more narrowly scoped before external plugins can depend on them.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Do not expose local assistant memory through Gateway until a different privacy or ownership model is defined.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Accept the provider-neutral, memory-only API with its current explicit selection, idempotency, workspace confinement, backup, and recovery guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the canonical feature proposal and the cross-cutting migration design, making them the best available person to coordinate the product and security decision.
